summary: Screen before solving, content-hash cache, parallel solves, coarse-to-fine re-solve and an in-process the in-house C++ solver (Eigen) screening path.

steps: 1. Key = sha256(design hash, mesh size, element order, solver version, spec hash).
2. Store Result and checks under runs/cache/<key>/; evaluate() returns the cached entry when the key exists.
3. Test that a repeated trial is served from cache in under 0.1 s.
verify: micromamba run -n attome-ae python -m pytest tests/test_cache.py -q
tasks.done_when: Repeated evaluations are cached and identical.
do_not: do not cache failed solves caused by timeouts
tasks.stop_and_ask_if: a cached result differs from a fresh solve.

tasks.task: Run evaluations in parallel and re-solve the front on a fine mesh.
steps: 1. Run trials with n_jobs equal to physical cores minus one, each ccx with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1.
2. verify_front(study) re-solves every Pareto design with mesh size halved and records the change in each objective.
3. Write evaluations per minute and the coarse-to-fine objective changes into docs/benchmarks.md.
verify: micromamba run -n attome-ae python -m structura.optimize.verify_front runs/demo
prints coarse vs fine objectives for each front design
tasks.done_when: Throughput and coarse-to-fine drift are measured and written down.
do_not: do not report coarse-mesh numbers as final
tasks.stop_and_ask_if: the front's ranking changes on the fine mesh for more than one design.

tasks.task: Add screening before solving and the the in-house C++ solver (Eigen) fast path.
steps: 1. evaluate() calls feasible() and gate() before meshing and returns status screened_out with the reason when either fails.
2. skfem_fast.solve(mesh, bc) assembles linear elasticity once per mesh topology and reuses the factorization across load cases.
3. Use skfem_fast for screening evaluations only; every front design is still solved by CalculiX.
4. Record evaluations per minute and cache hit rate for a 200-evaluation study in docs/benchmarks.md.
tasks.done_when: Screened designs cost milliseconds and throughput is measured.
do_not: do not report a the in-house C++ solver (Eigen) screening result as a final number
tasks.stop_and_ask_if: skfem_fast and CalculiX differ by more than 3% on the bracket.

acceptance: Cache, parallel run and fine re-solve in place
Screened-out designs never reach the mesher
Throughput and cache hit rate measured
risks: Parallel runs exhaust memory on fine meshes; fine re-solves run one at a time.
